statement: The function returns a result r. Let n = len(arr). For each integer k with 0 <= k <= n, define S_k = { arr[j] | 0 <= j < k } (the set of positions set to 1 after k steps). For 1 <= k <= n and 1 <= p <= n-m+1, say that [p, p+m-1] is a maximal group of ones of length m at step k iff: (a) for every q with p <= q <= p+m-1, q in S_k; (b) p = 1 or (p-1) not in S_k; (c) p+m-1 = n or (p+m) not in S_k. Say HasGroup(k) iff there exists p with 1 <= p <= n-m+1 satisfying (a)-(c). Then: if there exists an integer k with 1 <= k <= n and HasGroup(k), r is the maximum of { k | 1 <= k <= n and HasGroup(k) }; otherwise r = -1.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). We assume n >= 1. We assume 1 <= m <= n. We assume arr is a permutation of the integers 1..n: for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= arr[i] <= n; and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, arr[i] != arr[j]. All arithmetic in the problem (indices, steps) fits in 64-bit signed integers.
